title: Islanded fragment runner and lazy page-rewrite reclaim path
author: Sofia Chen
description: Motivation: production workloads showed repeated small free regions inside the KV cache after tenant churn and background lease expirations. The existing compaction path relied on aggressive whole-segment compaction, which created IO spikes and unfair eviction across tenants. This PR introduces an "islanded fragment runner" plus a lazy page-rewrite batcher to reduce fragmentation without large synchronous compaction windows. High-level goals: (1) isolate tiny fragments into 'islands' that are eligible for low-priority rewrite rather than immediate eviction, (2) introduce a staged evictor with tenant-aware pacing and soft-quarantine hysteresis so recently demoted pages are not immediately re-evicted, (3) add a low-priority rewrite-batcher that performs small in-place page rewrites/defrag cycles to coalesce islands during steady-state, and (4) expose runtime knobs and metrics to monitor island counts, rewrite latency, and tenant fairness. Change summary: - New islanded fragment lifecycle and bookkeeping (island id per region, demotion timestamps). - Lazy rewrite-batcher daemon that groups small fragments into batches sized by target_rewrite_bytes and respects a global IO budget. - Staged evictor: fast-path evictor for hot pressure, slow-path for island rewrite candidates, with tenant-weighted pacing to avoid tenant starvation. - KV allocator hint changes to prefer page-aligned placements for rewrite-friendly coalescing. - Telemetry: island_count, rewrite_batches, rewrite_bytes, tenant_rewrite_backlog, staged_evictor_cycles. Compatibility and safety: feature gated behind runtime flag kv.enable_islanded_rewrite=false by default. All changes are opt-in and can be toggled per deployment. Rollout plan: enable for internal canary with 1% traffic -> 10% -> 50% after two perf sweeps. Checklist: - [x] Implementation of islanded fragment tracker and allocator hints - [x] Lazy rewrite-batcher with IO budgeting and batch coalescer - [x] Staged evictor + tenant pacing loop - [x] Unit tests for island lifecycle and eviction paths - [x] Integration test harness simulating tenant churn and continuous batching - [x] Benchmarks against synthetic mixed-tenancy workload - [x] Documentation: runtime config docs and Console metric wiring Notes: description includes short rationale for design tradeoffs; see commit messages for micro design decisions and pointers to internal design doc (shared via Linear ENG-1842).

review_comments: 2024-11-18 Arjun Patel: Design looks promising; two asks - (1) add a hard upper bound on rewrite IO per tenant to avoid noisy neighbor, (2) add more defensive checks around island metadata lifecycle to avoid leaks.

2024-11-22 Evan Kim: Found a race in staged evictor where eviction token was not atomically transferred to slow-path. Requested an explicit CAS and test.
2024-11-24 Sofia Chen: Added CAS fix and a targeted multithreaded test simulating concurrent eviction + rewrite worker; CI flake observed and re-run passed.
2024-11-28 Marta Lopez: Verified telemetry and console widgets; left an approval after minor docs nit.
ci_checks: perf-regressions: bench_island_rewrite (passed, 12% median memory reclaimed without CPU increase)
release_notes: Add an opt-in KV islanded fragmentation handler and low-priority page rewrite batcher to reduce small-fragment eviction and long tail memory pressure. Disabled by default; runtime flag kv.enable_islanded_rewrite. Improves memory reclamation under multi-tenant churn with controlled IO budget.
tests: unit: islanded_tracker_test.cc (covers lifecycle, tombstone expiry, leak checks)
stress: kv_rewrite_stress (30m run on canary infra)
perf_benchmarks: Synthetic mixed-tenant run (10 tenants, write-heavy churn): median memory overhead reduced 12% and 95th-p99 memory pressure lowered 18% compared to baseline
Tail-latency: p99 write latency unchanged (+0.4ms noise) under enabled steady-state; compaction IO bursts reduced by 85%
Rewrite IO: average background IO increased by 6% but sustained no CPU regression in worker pool
risk_assessment: Medium: introduces background rewrite IO and new lifecycle state. Mitigations: feature-flagged rollout, per-tenant IO caps, tombstone sweeper, and presubmit + integration + stress tests. Monitoring dashboards added for island counts and tenant rewrite backlog.
notes: Design doc link: Linear ENG-1842 contains workload traces and offline simulations. Follow-up work: adaptive rewrite batch sizing based on observed sequence length distributions and kernel locality hints.
